BiblicalUsage: manʻam is a delicacy, a dainty, and it occurs once, in Psalms 141:4. There the psalmist prays that his heart not be inclined to any evil thing, to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity, and that he not eat of their dainties. The word is the rich food of wicked company, and the prayer refuses it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe manʻam warns me that the table I sit at shapes the heart I keep, and I will not trade my integrity for a dainty.
